examples.source:
"""Reads a Lantern library: who serves it, its apps, what a console is missing, and one verified download.

    python examples/read_library.py https://shelf.example.org/ [platform]

The download is checked against the SHA-256 the server lists and renamed only when it matches; a `.part`
file is resumed with a Range request after a cut (SPEC.md § 6.6).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import lantern


def main(url: str, platform: str = "switch") -> None:
    with lantern.LanternClient(url, platform=platform, user_agent="ReadLibrary/1.0") as client:
        hello = client.handshake()
        print(f"{hello.name}: {', '.join(sorted(hello.features))}")

        apps = list(client.iter_apps(page_size=5))  # every page, cursor by cursor
        for app in apps:
            print(f"  {app.name} {app.version_name or app.version_code} ({app.size} bytes)")

        # What a console that holds the first app, at version 0, is missing.
        if apps:
            page = client.missing([(apps[0].app_id, 0)], want=("update", "dlc"))
            print(f"missing: {len(page.items)} on the first page")

        # The smallest non-empty file, downloaded to a temporary folder and checked on the way.
        if apps:
            smallest = min((a for a in apps if a.size), key=lambda a: a.size)
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
                saved = client.download_app(smallest, Path(folder) / f"{smallest.app_id}.pkg")
                print(
                    f"downloaded {smallest.name}: {saved.stat().st_size} bytes, sha256 {smallest.sha256[:12]}… matched"
                )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    main(*sys.argv[1:3])

examples.title: Adds Lantern to a FastAPI app: the same one-game library as serve_flask.py
examples.source:
"""Adds Lantern to a FastAPI app: the same one-game library as serve_flask.py.

uvicorn --factory examples.serve_fastapi:make_app --port 8080
python examples/serve_fastapi.py 8080
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

from fastapi import FastAPI

from lantern.server import LanternApp, MemoryLibrary
from lantern.server.fastapi import include


def make_app() -> FastAPI:
    library = MemoryLibrary(base="/api/lantern")
    library.add_app_file(
        data=b"a made-up game",
        platform="switch",
        title_id="0100ABCD00010000",
        app_id="0100ABCD00010000",
        type="base",
        version_code=0,
        name="Frost Garden",
        format="nsp",
        version_name="1.0.0",
    )
    app = FastAPI()
    include(app, LanternApp(library, uid="3d5c7e1a-0b2f-4c6d-9e8a-1f2b3c4d5e6f", name="Living room shelf"))
    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn

    uvicorn.run(make_app(), host="127.0.0.1", port=int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8080)

examples.title: Adds Lantern to a Flask app: a library of one made-up game, served anonymously
examples.source:
"""Adds Lantern to a Flask app: a library of one made-up game, served anonymously.

    python examples/serve_flask.py 8080        # then: curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/.well-known/lantern

`MemoryLibrary` holds apps in memory; a real server implements `lantern.server.Library` over its own
files and database. For tokens, pairing and signed requests, pass `accounts=MemoryAccounts(...)`
(or an `authenticate` hook) to `LanternApp`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

from flask import Flask

from lantern.server import LanternApp, MemoryLibrary
from lantern.server.flask import init_app


def make_app() -> Flask:
    library = MemoryLibrary(base="/api/lantern")
    library.add_app_file(
        data=b"a made-up game",
        platform="switch",
        title_id="0100ABCD00010000",
        app_id="0100ABCD00010000",
        type="base",
        version_code=0,
        name="Frost Garden",
        format="nsp",
        version_name="1.0.0",
    )
    app = Flask(__name__)
    init_app(app, LanternApp(library, uid="3d5c7e1a-0b2f-4c6d-9e8a-1f2b3c4d5e6f", name="Living room shelf"))
    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    make_app().run(host="127.0.0.1", port=int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8080)

examples.title: A static library: a library written as JSON files (GitHub Pages, a NAS, a USB stick), then read back
examples.source:
"""A static library: a library written as JSON files (GitHub Pages, a NAS, a USB stick), then read back.

    python examples/static_library.py out/        # serve out/ with any web server, or open it as a folder

SPEC.md § 21. The files are the same documents a live server sends, with their SHA-256 and a handshake at
`lantern.json`, so a client reads them with no server code behind them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from lantern.server import MemoryLibrary
from lantern.static import StaticLibrary, export


def main(out: Path) -> None:
    library = MemoryLibrary(base="/api/lantern")
    library.add_app_file(
        data=b"a made-up game",
        platform="switch",
        title_id="0100ABCD00010000",
        app_id="0100ABCD00010000",
        type="base",
        version_code=0,
        name="Frost Garden",
        format="nsp",
        version_name="1.0.0",
    )
    summary = export(library, out, uid="3d5c7e1a-0b2f-4c6d-9e8a-1f2b3c4d5e6f", name="Shelf on a stick")
    print(f"wrote {summary}")
    with StaticLibrary(out) as shelf:
        print(shelf.handshake().name, [app.name for app in shelf.iter_apps("switch")])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        main(Path(sys.argv[1]))
    else:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            main(Path(folder) / "shelf")
